title: People Officer
description:
People Officer
Location: Seaham
Hours: 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Duration: 12 weeks minimum
Start: As soon as possible

Are you an experienced HR professional looking for a varied generalist role where you can make a real impact?

We are recruiting for a People Officer to join a friendly, supportive and forward-thinking organisation based in Seaham.
Working as part of the People team and alongside the Head of People, you will provide a proactive and professional HR service across the organisation. This is a varied, hands-on position that would suit someone who enjoys building relationships, supporting managers and getting involved across the full employee life cycle.

The role

As People Officer, you will:
- Provide advice and support to managers and senior leaders on a range of HR matters
- Support recruitment and selection activity from start to finish
- Process contractual changes and maintain accurate employee records
- Provide guidance around HR policies, procedures, pay and conditions
- Coordinate payroll information with a third-party payroll provider
- Support employee meetings, including taking notes where required
- Help promote employee benefits and support employee queries
- Maintain accurate HR data and utilise HR systems effectively
- Support the implementation and continuous improvement of new People systems and processes

About you

We are looking for someone with:
- Previous generalist HR/People experience
- Experience managing or coordinating recruitment processes
- A good working knowledge of HR policies, procedures and processes
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
- Excellent attention to detail and confidence working with systems and data
- Strong interpersonal skills and the confidence to work with employees and senior stakeholders
- A flexible, hands-on approach and willingness to support across the wider People function
- CIPD Level 3 or relevant equivalent experience

This is a fantastic opportunity for an HR professional who enjoys variety and wants to join a collaborative and supportive People team where they can genuinely contribute to the development of the HR service.

Interested?

Apply today or get in touch with Lorna Jordinson at Hays for a confidential conversation.

title: Recruitment Administrator
description:
Recruitment Administrator (Temporary Assignment - 4 Months)
Sedgefield On-site 13.45 per hour
About the Role

We are seeking a Recruitment Administrator to join a busy recruitment team on a 6-month temporary assignment, providing essential support across a high-volume recruitment function.
This is a fast-paced, process-driven role that would suit someone who enjoys working with people, thrives in a busy environment, and takes pride in delivering excellent customer service. You will play a key role in supporting candidates, hiring managers, and recruitment partners throughout the recruitment process, ensuring a professional and efficient experience for all stakeholders.

What You'll Be Responsible For:

Recruitment Administration
- Manage recruitment-related enquiries and act as a first point of contact for candidates and hiring managers
- Coordinate interviews and support recruitment activities across multiple vacancies
- Maintain accurate recruitment records and candidate information
- Support onboarding and pre-employment screening processes

Systems & Data Management
- Work extensively with Microsoft Office applications, including:
- Outlook
- Excel
- Microsoft Lists
- Coordinate and maintain job advertisements across the intranet, careers website, and external online platforms
- Raise purchase orders using Microsoft D365
- Maintain trackers, records, and recruitment reports
- Ensure all data is accurate, up-to-date, and confidential

Customer Service & Stakeholder Support
- Deliver a responsive and customer-focused service to candidates, managers, and external partners
- Build positive relationships across the business
- Keep stakeholders informed throughout the recruitment process
- Support the successful delivery of recruitment activities within a fast-paced HR environment.

Administrative Support
- Process recruitment documentation accurately and efficiently
- Support invoice processing and purchase order administration
- Assist with reporting and recruitment metrics where required

About You
You are organised, resilient, and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly.
You'll bring:
- Experience working in a busy office or administrative environment
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Outlook, Teams and Excel
- Excellent attention to detail and data accuracy
- Strong communication and customer service skills
- Confidence using business systems and learning new processes quickly

Desirable (but not essential):
- Experience of Microsoft D365 or similar systems
- Experience of Microsoft Lists
- Experience within recruitment, HR, or administration
- Experience processing purchase orders or invoices

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who:
- Enjoys helping people
- Remains calm under pressure
- Is positive, proactive, and adaptable
- Takes pride in delivering a great service

Why Join Us?
- Opportunity to build your recruitment experience in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.
- Varied role with exposure to different stakeholders and processes
- Supportive and collaborative environment
- Immediate opportunity to make an impact
- Competitive hourly rate ( 13.45 per hour)

Location & Working Pattern
- Based in Sedgefield, based onsite
- 37 hours per week
- Monday-Thursday: 08:30 - 17:00, Friday: 08:30 - 16:30

The Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organised administrator who enjoys working with people and delivering excellent customer service. If you're looking for a busy, varied role where you can make an immediate contribution, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Candidate Manager / Resourcer
description:
Candidate Manager / Resourcer

Newcastle Children's Education Services (CES) Education Recruitment Career Progression

Are you passionate about people, relationship building, and making a real difference to young people's lives?

At Prospero Teaching, we've been connecting exceptional education professionals with schools, local authorities and education providers for over 20 years. As part of our growing Children's Education Services (CES) division, we're looking for a Candidate Manager / Resourcer to join our Newcastle team.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and wants to play a key role in supporting vulnerable children through the placement of high-quality tutors and education professionals.

About the Role

As a Candidate Manager / Resourcer, you will be responsible for attracting, sourcing and managing a network of tutors and education professionals who deliver specialist support to children and young people.

Working closely with the Account Management team, you'll ensure we have the right candidates available to meet client requirements while providing an outstanding candidate experience throughout the recruitment journey.

Key Responsibilities
- Source, attract and engage high-quality tutors and education professionals
- Manage candidate applications and conduct initial interviews and screenings
- Build and maintain a strong candidate talent pool
- Match suitable candidates to client requirements
- Manage candidate compliance and onboarding processes
- Develop strong relationships with candidates throughout their journey
- Maintain accurate records using internal systems and databases
- Work collaboratively with Account Managers to fulfil vacancies efficiently
- Support tutors throughout their placements, ensuring a positive experience

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience within recruitment, resourcing, talent acquisition, customer service, sales or account management
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Ability to work in a fast-paced, target-driven environment
- A proactive and positive attitude
- Strong administrative and IT skills
- A genuine passion for helping people and making a difference

What's in it for You?
- Competitive basic salary
- Uncapped bonus and commission opportunities
- Industry-leading training and development
- Clear career progression opportunities
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the lives of vulnerable children and young people

Why Prospero Teaching?

At Prospero Teaching, we're passionate about connecting the right people with the right opportunities. Every placement we make helps support children and young people to reach their full potential.

If you're looking for a rewarding career where you can combine relationship building, recruitment and purpose-driven work, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and start your next chapter with Prospero Teaching.

title: Compliance Administrator - Leading Recruitment Company
description:
Join Prospero Teaching - Where Passion Meets Purpose in Education!

For over 20 years, Prospero Teaching has been a trusted leader in connecting teaching and support staff with schools, academies, and nurseries across the UK and internationally. We proudly offer our services to a broad range of educational settings, including EYFS, Primary, Secondary, Further Education, SEN, and PRUs.

About the Role

As a Compliance Administrator, you will be a key member of our compliance team, responsible for ensuring candidates meet the necessary regulatory and internal requirements to work within the education sector. You will play a vital role in maintaining compliance with industry standards and fostering a smooth recruitment process for candidates.

Key Responsibilities
- Collaborate with the compliance team to ensure candidates meet all compliance standards for the education sector.
- Follow established operational processes and procedures to ensure adherence to regulations and industry standards.
- Guide and support candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Conduct compliance checks, including but not limited to right-to-work, DBS, reference, and employment history verifications.
- Maintain and update accurate candidate records.
- Organise and verify candidate documentation.
- Respond to both internal and external inquiries efficiently and professionally.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented individual with:
- A good general education (minimum GCSEs in Maths and English, grades A-C, or equivalent).
- Strong relationship-building skills.
- The ability to work effectively under deadlines.
- Excellent administrative and organizational abilities, with a talent for prioritizing tasks.
- Strong communication and customer service skills.
- An understanding of confidentiality and data protection.
- A proactive problem-solving mindset.
- A commitment to safeguarding practices.

Benefits
- Competitive salary with a commission structure.
- Ongoing training and opportunities for professional development.
- Clear career advancement prospects within the company.
- A dynamic and collaborative work environment.
- Private healthcare.
- Quarterly performance-based incentives.

Join us and be part of a team that's helping drive one of the UK's fastest-growing recruitment firms forward.

title: Delivery Consultant/Resourcer
description:
Working from our head office in Hoults Yard, Newcastle Upon Tyne, you will support our team of dedicated multi-discipline recruitment consultants as a Delivery Consultant in one of our divisions; Rail, Built Environment and Facilities Management.

As a Delivery Consultant you will be responsible for resourcing candidates for both immediate and ongoing client needs. In speaking to candidates, building relationships and growing your specialist network you will cover the full recruitment process from start to finish.

We have a successful track record of developing our Delivery Consultants into expert recruiters. In this role, you can enter an industry with unlimited opportunities, learn from the best and develop your skills in a dynamic, supportive and fast-paced environment.

What are your responsibilities as a Delivery Consultant?
- Resourcing candidates for live jobs, to include database and job site searches, advertising and networking
- Contacting previously identified candidates to check availability for specific assignments
- On-going generation of marketable candidates by advertising, mail shots, headhunting, referrals and events
- Overall maintenance of database candidate files ensuring all information is entered and updated on a regular basis
- Registering new candidates in line with company administrative and legislative requirements
- Formatting CVs as required
- Responsible for identifying and informing consultants of potential sales leads gained from registration forms, references taken and conversations with candidates
- Arranging candidate interviews with clients, issuing confirmation letters/emails and briefing notes where relevant
- Placing job adverts onto relevant job sites, ensuring that all adverts comply with company and legal requirements
- Responding to incoming enquiries in a courteous and timely manner
- Ensuring a proactive and consistent service level for all clients through effective candidate matching and maintaining a professional approach at all times
- Ensuring a consistent level of service to all candidates by maintaining contact, updating them about their application and acting as an ambassador for the brand
- Adhoc projects and general administrative support
- Achievements of agreed KPIs and targets
- Be aware of and adhere to all policies and procedures, in particular the Company s Health & Safety, Modern Slavery and GDPR Polices

About You
No prior recruitment experience is required. We re looking for articulate & tenacious candidates who have:
- The basics: excellent communication, time management and organisational skills
- A keen focus on delivering outstanding customer service
- Strong attention to detail
- Great team skills, takes initiative and can work independently
- A friendly and professional manner
- Proficient IT / Microsoft Office skills

What are the benefits?
- Realise your true potential with a clear professional development plan
- Dedicated training with our experienced team
- Quarterly / monthly incentive schemes (hard work is recognised and rewarded)
- Holiday allowance
- A contemporary, modern office environment
- Unlimited earning potential
- 24/7 confidential support helpline
- Private healthcare insurance

description:
French-Speaking Strategic Sourcer

6 Months Contract

Newcastle hybrid working - can be remote

Native or C1/C2 Fluent French & Fluent English

Are you a proactive recruitment, sourcing, or sales professional who excels at finding hidden talent? Do you speak fluent French and want to play a key role in driving European hiring growth for a major global professional services firm?

We are seeking a French-Speaking Strategic Sourcer to join an established recruitment hub in Newcastle. In this role, you will act as the driving engine behind top-of-funnel talent discovery, partnering with recruiters and hiring managers to engage high-calibre candidates across the French market.

You will be responsible for
- Talent Sourcing: Develop and execute creative outreach strategies across LinkedIn, job boards, and professional networks to identify passive tech and consulting talent in France.
- Candidate Engagement & Screening: Conduct initial telephone and video interviews in French and English to evaluate candidates' skills, background, and cultural fit.
- Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner directly with recruiters and business leaders to define target candidate profiles and deliver detailed shortlist briefs.
- Pipeline Management: Build and maintain an active talent pool for both current hiring needs and future headcount demands.
- Data & Recruitment Analytics: Keep applicant tracking systems (ATS) up-to-date and monitor key outreach conversion metrics to optimize sourcing channels.

Essential Skills
- Full professional fluency in both French and English (written and verbal).
- Proven track record in candidate sourcing, talent acquisition, or agency recruitment.
- Familiarity with Boolean search syntax, candidate databases, and ATS tools.
- Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to engage passive candidates confidently.
- Based in or near Newcastle upon Tyne (or willing to travel for key on-site training and team meetings),

title: People Coordinator
description:
Belmont Recruitment are currently seeking an experienced People Coordinator to work with our client on a temporary basis. This is an initial two-month role working 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday, based in the Washington area.

Overview:

Reporting to the Recruitment Advisor, the People Coordinator will support recruitment and selection activity, equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) initiatives, positive action programmes and the day-to-day administration and user support of the iTrent HR information system.

The role will support the recruitment and onboarding for the organisation, helping to promote fair, inclusive and accessible employment opportunities. Responsibilities will also include maintaining accurate HR data, producing workforce reports and supporting improvements to recruitment processes, HR systems and workforce diversity.

Main Duties:
- Coordinate end-to-end recruitment and selection processes, including recruitment campaigns, vacancy advertising, shortlisting, interviews, assessments and pre-employment checks
- Provide recruitment advice and guidance to managers, candidates and other stakeholders, responding to enquiries and supporting effective recruitment processes
- Support recruitment attraction, outreach and engagement activities, including positive action initiatives aimed at attracting underrepresented groups
- Build effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support recruitment objectives and workforce diversity
- Contribute to EDI initiatives, Equality Impact Assessments and organisational action plans, helping to promote inclusive recruitment and employment practices
- Monitor recruitment and workforce equality data, prepare reports, identify trends and present findings to support decision-making and improve representation
- Maintain accurate people records and recruitment information, supporting effective system administration and data quality

Essential Criteria:
- CIPD Level 3 qualification or equivalent relevant experience within an HR environment
- Experienced user of iTrent system
- Previous experience in end-to-end, high-volume recruitment and selection, including onboarding and pre-employment checks
- Previous experience of working on recruitment campaigns, candidate attraction, outreach activities or positive action initiatives
- Experience in providing recruitment advice and guidance to managers, candidates or other stakeholders

If your skills match the above criteria, please apply with your up-to-date CV!
